words.translation: short daily team meeting (≈15 min) where each member reports progress, blockers and next steps

words.translation: a unit of work in your project tracker (Jira, Linear, etc.)

words.example: I think I need to dig deeper into our JWT library.

a pre-production environment used to test before release
words.example: I'll push the initial version to our staging environment this afternoon.

words.translation: an uncommon scenario that exposes hidden bugs
a critical bug that blocks the release

slides.content:
A standup is a fast, repetitive format. Every developer answers three questions:
• What did I work on?
• What am I working on now?
• Am I blocked on anything?

Notice four patterns in the clip — they are the building blocks you will use every morning:
• Present perfect continuous (I have been + -ing) → ongoing work since yesterday
• Run into / dig deeper into → describing problems and how you are tackling them
• Hedging language (kind of / sort of / I think / maybe) → expressing uncertainty politely
• Future intent (I will / I am going to / I will keep + -ing) → next steps
slides.title: Standup language patterns
slides.teacherNotes: Drill the four patterns orally before the controlled practice. Encourage the student to swap nouns (auth service → API endpoint, deployment, dashboard) so the patterns become reusable.

words.word: I've been working on the new authentication service.
words.example: Pattern: I have been + -ing  (since yesterday / this week)
Pattern: run into / dig deeper into / look into
words.word: I've run into some issues with token refresh.

words.example: Pattern: I am not sure but… / it might / I think / maybe
words.word: I'm not sure but it might be related to how we're handling asynchronous actions.

words.example: Pattern: I will + verb  /  I will keep + -ing  /  I am going to + verb
words.word: I'll keep working on the token validation logic.

slides.subtitle: Use the four standup patterns to build the sentences.

slides.prompt: Imagine you are at tomorrow morning's standup. Give your update in 60–90 seconds.
slides.content:
Pick a real or hypothetical project you are working on.
Report ONE thing you worked on yesterday  (use: I have been + -ing).
Report ONE blocker  (use: I have run into… / I am waiting for…).
Hedge ONE uncertainty  (use: I am not sure but… / it might…).
State ONE thing you will do next  (use: I will… / I am going to…).
Speak for ~60–90 seconds. Then swap to the teacher's role and ask one follow-up question.
